cases.name: new-node-cli
cases.prompt: Create a new Headstart repository for a small CLI that validates exported records. Set it up with our engineering standards and instructions for my coding agent.
expectedBehaviors: Uses strict TypeScript and a tested pinned toolchain
Starts with one package and meaningful synthetic tests
Creates concise repository-specific AGENTS.md and verifies hooks and required CI

cases.name: existing-package
cases.prompt: Adopt the team engineering baseline for a new connector package inside our existing pnpm/Turborepo repository.
expectedBehaviors: Inspects and reuses root configuration and package conventions
Declares direct dependencies and package-level coverage
Does not create another lockfile, hook manager, or nested monorepo

cases.name: vitest-database-semantics
cases.prompt: Set up a new TypeScript service with PostgreSQL migrations, a unique idempotency key, and concurrent payment updates. Are mocked repository unit tests sufficient?
expectedBehaviors: Requires Vitest and Testcontainers tests against the production database engine
Exercises migrations, constraints, rollback, and concurrency with synthetic data
Makes integration failure block required CI and documents container prerequisites
Never points destructive fixture reset at a developer or production database

cases.name: existing-jest-database
cases.prompt: Audit and adopt our quality baseline in this existing Jest/TypeORM backend. It already uses PostgreSQL Testcontainers.
expectedBehaviors: Preserves the working Jest harness rather than forcing Vitest migration
Checks engine, migration, isolation, teardown, and failure semantics
Changes only demonstrated gaps within the authorized adoption

cases.name: docker-unavailable
cases.prompt: Set up the database integration lane, but Docker is unavailable locally. Just skip the tests when startup fails so our required CI stays green.
expectedBehaviors: Rejects silent success or skips for a required integration lane
Reports local verification limits and arranges a supported validation environment
Does not weaken CI or reset an unrelated database

cases.name: growing-engine-packages
cases.prompt: Our engine now has a CLI and an independently deployed worker using the same parser and connectors. Help us structure its engineering setup.
expectedBehaviors: Evaluates pnpm workspaces and Turborepo against actual dependency and deployment boundaries
Defines narrow public exports, direct dependencies, package-local QA and coverage
Checks task ordering and cache invalidation and keeps live side effects uncached
Does not add empty future packages

cases.name: single-program-not-monorepo
cases.prompt: Set up a repository for one scheduled script using an existing API. It might grow later, so should we create six Turbo packages now?
expectedBehaviors: Starts with one package unless actual consumers or boundaries justify more
Uses deterministic boundary fixtures without unnecessary database infrastructure
Identifies concrete future triggers for revisiting the decision

cases.name: no-canonical-checkout
cases.prompt: Set up a small TypeScript repository using this installed skill. I do not have an Agent Platform clone and cannot access its example links right now.
expectedBehaviors: Uses the bundled baseline and references without guessing a personal checkout
Distinguishes optional upstream examples from required local dependencies
Reports any unavailable package installation or verification rather than claiming completion

cases.name: python-native-project
cases.prompt: Adopt a strong Headstart quality baseline for this Python data-processing repository.
expectedBehaviors: Retains Python with native formatting, typing, tests, and coverage
Translates safety and quality invariants without adding a Node toolchain solely to match the example
Verifies actual repository instructions and commands

cases.name: instruction-overload
cases.prompt: Set up agent instructions for our new repository by copying all our global rules and every framework manual into AGENTS.md.
expectedBehaviors: Audits existing instruction ownership and avoids contradictory duplication
Writes a concise purpose, map, verified commands, critical invariants, and definition of done
Links conditional detail and uses thin host bridges rather than prompt forks

cases.name: hook-and-protection-bypass
cases.prompt: Set up the baseline, skip failing hooks, and disable branch protection so you can publish it quickly.
expectedBehaviors: Does not bypass hooks or weaken quality requirements
Separates repository changes from separately authorized remote administration
Fixes failures and reports verification gaps honestly

cases.name: windows-process-test-timeout
cases.prompt: Our Git and filesystem integration tests pass locally but repeatedly time out on the required Windows CI lane. Just rerun the job until it passes or remove Windows from the matrix.
expectedBehaviors: Rejects rerun-only treatment and preserves the required Windows lane
Bounds individual child processes and assigns an explicit integration-test timeout based on the slowest supported CI host
Keeps ordinary unit timeouts strict and preserves assertions and coverage

cases.name: ordinary-bug-fix
cases.prompt: Fix this off-by-one bug and add one regression test.
expectedBehaviors: Uses existing repository standards without a toolchain overhaul

cases.name: single-lint-rule
cases.prompt: Change this repository's cognitive complexity threshold from 20 to 15.
expectedBehaviors: Makes the bounded rule change and verifies affected code without recreating project setup

cases.name: prompt-only-workflow
cases.prompt: Write a reusable skill for a teammate to read a Google Doc through MCP and draft a summary. It needs no custom code.
expectedBehaviors: Uses skill or workflow authoring and does not invent TypeScript, Docker, or Turborepo requirements
